I've been working this land for thirty years, and Quzhou soil knows cotton — that's what I know too. My 9 mu has to feed six mouths and still bring in cash. Some of my children work in the city now, which helps, but I still need the farm to pull its weight. Wheat goes in the ground every autumn — we eat it ourselves, and what's left over sells. After wheat comes off in June, I put maize in the same fields without wasting time. Cotton gets the best share of my land — it earns the most cash.

I don't use fancy techniques. I plough before cotton and wheat, rotary or skip tillage when putting maize in after wheat harvest since there's no time to waste. I've switched to improved cotton seed — the Bt kind my neighbors use. Saves me some spraying for bollworm. For wheat and maize I use the hybrid seed the village supply co-op sells. I fertilize by feel mostly, but I put more nitrogen on wheat and maize than cotton — that's what gives yield. My well pump handles irrigation. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll set. Wheat I water at jointing and heading. Maize I try to water at tasseling if it's dry.
